_comment: Pins `isArabicQuoteLine` across its copies: scripts/lib/book-html.mjs (the PDF and
the Composer's Read view), src/lib/reader/markdown.ts (the on-screen reader), and
Neither renderer was pinned to the other before 2026-08-09. Both asked only whether
a quotation line CONTAINED Arabic, so an English translation carrying the (ع)
honorific after Ali's name was set right-to-left in the Arabic face. A one-sided fix
would have given the printed page and the reader different directions for the same
paragraph, which is the one divergence no gate here could see.
`arabic` is the expected answer: true means the line is set RTL in the Arabic face,
false means it is a translation.

cases.text: إِنَّ عَلِيًّا مَعَ الْقُرْآنِ وَالْقُرْآنُ مَعَ عَلِيٍّ، لَنْ يَفْتَرِقَا حَتَّى يَرِدَا عَلَيَّ الْحَوْضَ

cases.why: a SHORT Arabic quotation — isArabicOnlyParagraph would demote this to a translation
the defect: an English translation carrying the (ع) honorific
cases.text: "Ali is with the Quran and the Quran is with Ali (ع). They will not separate from each other until they return to me at the pool."

cases.why: the worst instance found: an editorial note flipped by three root letters
cases.text: **Editorial note (tradition-grounded).** A related teaching names ihsan as the highest form of a single root, ح-س-ن, in which goodness and beauty are one word.

cases.why: the mandated Prophet ligature must not flip an English line either
cases.text: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said this to his companions on the day of the farewell.

cases.why: plain English with no Arabic at all
cases.text: They will not separate from each other until they return to me at the pool.

cases.why: an Arabic line carrying a bare verse locator — digits are not Latin letters
an Arabic run beside a long transliteration reads as the translation line
cases.text: قول (qawl) is the word used here, and it carries the sense of an utterance rather than a mere sound
